fixed.how: (1) CriticLoop.filesOfTask: the review's changed files are now the task's files over all its attempts: this run's, plus the task.files events in the sessions of the task's runs. When a run changed nothing, the evidence says 'attempt N changed no file; …'. An open 'Check failed' finding makes the project's checks run whatever changed. A page named by an open 'Tried' finding is tried again first. (2) New file packages/critic/src/measured.ts (measuredFindingOf, resolvedByRerun). A finding the runtime measured ('Check failed: <name>' or 'Tried <page>: <problem>') is resolved only when this review's verification record shows a passing re-run, whatever the verdict. An accept does not resolve it, and neither does the model's resolved list. An accept while such a finding is still open is refused by the store as before (B.4) and leads to the existing 'rework, accept or cancel' card. (3) Decision on failures the task did not cause. Pages: the try now records pageFiles, the folder files the page asked for (capabilities try-page.ts). attributeTry treats an error on a page that opened as the task's blocker only when the task changed one of the files that run on that page; stylesheets, images and fonts run nothing. Otherwise the problem becomes a low finding '… (not caused by this task)', the try's output says so, and the person sees it under 'See what was checked'. Tests: code cannot tell whose change broke a test, so the failure still blocks. The failed-check finding now asks the specialist: 'if it failed before this task, say so and why under "Questions for the person:"'. That report goes to the person as one question card (the existing U-022 path) instead of a ladder of reruns. (4) Found while writing the real-daemon case: the daemon's PATH had npm but the review's sandbox lease did not, so 'spawn npm ENOENT' failed the whole review. npm is now probed inside the lease ('npm --version'). A check whose command cannot start is a failed check with the reason as its output, not a failed review. All of this is recorded in ADR 0104 point 9 and its Consequences.

notes_for_other_areas: verification (owns the review path in runner.ts): the review-failed branch now does the following. If the session's own controller is aborted and the person did not move the task, an in_review task goes back to ready with `restoreStatus(…, 'in_review', reason)`, `runningTask` is set and `killed` is thrown. A task the person moved records `recordMove(now, 'review_failed', 'review', stoppedByMove(reviewController))` first. Keep both. taskDisplay (daemon/task-words.ts): in_review with a retry-kind card is key 'answer', label 'Needs your decision', blocker cardKind 'retry'. apps/ui actionsFor: key 'answer' with status in_review gives ['answer','cancel'] (Try again is not offered: in_review → ready is no graph edge).

session engine: `recordMove(t, outcome, during, stopped)` now takes `stopped`; work is set aside only when it is true. After a run, the move is recorded before the session's stop only when the person's move stopped the run first (`stoppedByMove`). session/recovery.ts `reviewBackToReady`: a released task still in_review goes to ready unless a holding card is open, and only tasks actually ready again are named in the summary and Update.

commands: `CommandPorts.stopTask` now returns `boolean | undefined` (whether a live run or review was stopped); `moveSentence`'s `work` follows it. Any new port implementation must return `kill.stopTask(...).stoppedRuns > 0` or the cancel line says only 'Cancelled "X".'

fixed.how: New capability packages/capabilities/src/web (policy.ts, fetch.ts): web_fetch reads one page by its address with a GET over node:http(s). Rules: http(s) only, at most 2,000 characters, no user name or password in the address, no cookie or authorisation header. The project's block list (settings.browser.blockedDomains) refuses a host whatever else says. A host on the project's site list (settings.browser.allowedDomains) is read wherever it points. Any other host is read only while every address it resolves to is public. That check runs in the client's lookup on the addresses the socket actually uses, so a name resolving to a private address, DNS rebinding and IP literals are refused too. Redirects are followed hop by hop through the same rules (at most 5). Limits: 2 MiB decompressed, 30 s, and the run's own stop. HTML goes through the browser's extractor; text, JSON, XML, CSV and markdown pass as they are; other types are refused in words.
